title: Photonics Forces A Chiplet Rethink
gist: As hyperscalers push co-packaged optics into advanced packages to beat copper's bandwidth/power/reach limits, moving photonic chiplets closer to compute silicon via hybrid bonding turns packaging into a bidirectional thermal, mechanical, and verification co-design problem; TSMC's COUPE platform, Ayar Labs/Alchip's 100 Tb/s UCIe demo, and NVIDIA's copper-now/optics-later Rubin-to-Feynman roadmap mark where the industry actually stands.

themes.theme: Photonics as a bidirectional system co-design problem

insights.claim: Photonics changes chiplet design from a placement problem into a multi-physics co-design problem, because thermal, mechanical, electromagnetic, and optical effects interact bidirectionally between the photonic and electronic dies once they share a package.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Reframes optical integration as a cross-disciplinary design problem rather than a swap-in interconnect upgrade, raising design cost, tooling requirements, and time-to-market risk for anyone deploying co-packaged optics, and favoring EDA vendors with full-stack multi-physics simulation capability.
insights.quote: The chip architect cannot think of it as an independent chiplet
insights.locator: The chip architect cannot think of it as an independent chiplet

insights.claim: The closer an optical chiplet is placed to compute silicon, the greater the bandwidth and power-efficiency gains, but the harder it becomes to manage heat, mechanical stress, alignment, and reliability.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Establishes the central engineering trade-off investors should use to evaluate any CPO product claim: proximity gains in performance come paired with proportionally higher integration and reliability risk that must be priced into adoption timelines.
insights.locator: The closer optics is to the processing elements, the lower the latency

insights.claim: With hybrid bonding removing the interposer and solder balls that previously separated electronic and photonic dies, the photonic chiplet becomes both a heat-generating aggressor toward the neighboring electronic chip and a temperature-sensitive victim of it, since photonic waveguide properties require thermal tuning and are highly sensitive to temperature variation.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Hybrid bonding, the packaging approach vendors are racing toward for performance reasons, simultaneously creates a new bidirectional thermal failure mode that most teams historically evaluated only one direction (electronics generating heat, not receiving thermal feedback from optics).
insights.quote: the photonic chiplet is both an aggressor and a victim in that new system
insights.locator: the photonic chiplet is both an aggressor and a victim

insights.claim: A formally verified digital/electrical interface contract, such as a UCIe adapter that can be proven free of deadlock and protocol violations using formal methods, is typically wrapped around an optical subsystem that has no comparable formal-verification discipline yet, an asymmetry that should concern system architects.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Points to an underappreciated verification gap: teams may be over-trusting optical subsystems relative to the rigor applied to their digital interfaces, a latent quality/reliability risk as CPO moves from prototype to volume production.
insights.quote: That asymmetry, a formally verified electrical contract wrapped around an informally specified optical subsystem, should worry system architects.
insights.locator: One die boundary is now a physical-domain conversion

insights.claim: Silicon micro-ring resonators used in photonic chiplets shift wavelength by roughly 70 to 80 picometers per degree Celsius, and a recent Advanced Photonics Nexus review found that even modest temperature variation across a wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) array causes enough drift and crosstalk that active thermal control is now standard practice in co-packaged optics designs.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Quantifies exactly how thermally fragile optical components are, explaining why active thermal control is now a mandatory (not optional) line item in CPO bill-of-materials and system design, a cost and complexity factor for anyone modeling CPO economics.
insights.locator: silicon micro-rings shift roughly 70 to 80 pm/

insights.claim: In co-packaged optics designs, the dominant heat source affecting photonic performance is usually the neighboring compute ASIC rather than the photonic die itself, which is why CPO architectures require thermal isolation, active stabilization, and sometimes package-level micro-coolers.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Shifts the thermal-management burden of CPO onto compute-die power management rather than the optics vendor alone, meaning packaging and compute-silicon teams must co-design thermal budgets jointly rather than treating optics as a bolt-on module.
insights.locator: The worst heat source is usually the neighboring compute ASIC

themes.theme: Packaging architecture roadmap: 2.5D interposer vs. 3D vertical stacking

insights.claim: TSMC's Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE), an open infrastructure for mass-producing optical chiplets, stacks the electronic control chip directly on top of the optical chiplet using hybrid bonding with copper-to-copper connections instead of placing the two chips side by side with solder balls; TSMC says this reduces the distance signals must travel, shrinks electrical parasitic resistance to near zero, cuts data transmission power consumption by up to 85%, and optimizes server space for high-density AI clusters.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: An 85% power-consumption cut for data transmission is a large, specific, vendor-quantified efficiency claim directly relevant to AI-datacenter power budgets; it's the concrete number to track as COUPE-based products reach production and independent validation.
insights.locator: TSMC introduced Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE)

insights.claim: In a 2.5D architecture, compute, memory, electronic-interface, and photonic chiplets are placed side by side on a silicon interposer, organic substrate, or advanced redistribution layer; this is the more mature, lower-risk approach that reuses standard interposer/RDL processes and lets the same photonic chiplet be reused across different compute dies, but the electrical trace length between the electronic interface chip and the photonic chip adds parasitic capacitance and inductance that caps how fast the modulators can be driven.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: 2.5D remains the lower-risk, near-term commercial path because it preserves chiplet reusability across compute-die generations, a relevant factor for assessing which vendors can ship CPO products fastest versus which are betting on riskier 3D integration.
insights.locator: in a 2.5D architecture, the compute, memory, electronic-interface

insights.claim: In a 3D stacked implementation, bonding the electronic interface die directly above or below the photonic die using micro bumps or copper-to-copper hybrid bonding shortens the electrical link between driver circuits and modulators/photodetectors from millimeters to microns, enabling higher baud rates at lower drive voltage and power per bit; this is the direction most co-packaged-optics roadmaps at Intel, TSMC (COUPE), Ayar Labs, and Broadcom are heading.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Naming four specific vendors converging on the same 3D-stacking direction signals where competitive R&D and capex is concentrating in CPO packaging, useful for tracking which suppliers are positioned to lead the next interconnect performance step.
insights.locator: This shortens the electrical link between driver circuits and modulators

insights.claim: TSMC, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries, STMicroelectronics, and Tower Semiconductor are all manufacturing photonics chips today, with STMicroelectronics in Europe pursuing a hybrid-bond strategy that places the electronic IC directly on top of the photonic IC.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A named list of five foundries already shipping photonics chips confirms optical integration has moved from lab research to active multi-vendor production, broadening the competitive and supply-chain map for photonics-exposed investors beyond just TSMC.
insights.locator: In addition to TSMC, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries, STMicroelectronics, and Tower Semiconductor

insights.claim: Ayar Labs' TeraPHY chiplet offers a UCIe-compliant electrical interface with 8 Tbps of bidirectional optical bandwidth, and a demonstration by Alchip and Ayar Labs on TSMC's COUPE platform delivers up to 100 Tb/s per accelerator behind a standard UCIe interface.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A concrete 100 Tb/s per-accelerator bandwidth figure behind a standard UCIe interface is a hard commercialization data point showing optical chiplet bandwidth is already an order of magnitude beyond typical electrical die-to-die links, relevant for gauging near-term AI accelerator I/O roadmaps.
insights.locator: Ayar Labs' TeraPHY offers a UCIe-compliant electrical interface

insights.claim: The UCIe Consortium has grown to more than 120 members and now treats optical interconnect as a core vertical within the standard, alongside its existing electrical die-to-die specification.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Formal standards-body adoption of optical interconnect as a core vertical, with 120+ member companies, reduces fragmentation risk and signals the industry expects optical chiplets to become a mainstream, interoperable building block rather than a proprietary niche.
insights.locator: the UCIe Consortium, over 120 members strong

themes.theme: Proximity-driven coexistence and the rack-scale roadmap

insights.claim: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang summarized the industry's current design philosophy at Computex 2026 as 'You use optics wherever you must. You use copper wherever you can,' reflecting a pattern of proximity-driven coexistence between optical and electrical interconnect rather than optics replacing copper outright.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A direct framing from the industry's dominant AI-compute vendor sets the baseline expectation that copper remains the default and optics is deployed selectively where reach or bandwidth truly requires it, tempering overly aggressive optics-replaces-copper narratives.
insights.quote: You use optics wherever you must. You use copper wherever you can.
insights.locator: Jensen Huang said it well at Computex 2026

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Rubin platform still uses copper for in-rack NVLink, with co-packaged optical NVLink not expected to arrive until around 2028 with the Feynman platform; intra-package reach is expected to stay electrical indefinitely, while package-to-package and rack-scale reach is where the shift to optics is already real and no longer a networking decision made after the silicon is designed.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Gives investors a specific named-platform timeline (Rubin now, Feynman circa 2028) for when NVIDIA's own interconnect roadmap shifts to optical NVLink, a concrete date to track against actual product launches and a proxy for broader CPO adoption timing in AI infrastructure.
insights.locator: NVIDIA's Rubin platform still uses copper for in-rack NVLink

insights.claim: The near-term trajectory for optical interconnect is to displace pluggable modules at the edge of the package for scale-up and scale-out links while electrical handles compute and short-reach connections; over time that boundary is expected to move inward toward compute, with the endgame being rack-scale disaggregation where pooled memory and large coherent or semi-coherent domains let a full rack, or several racks, behave like one large system.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Describes a multi-year architectural endpoint (rack-scale disaggregation via optical interconnect) that reshapes how AI infrastructure vendors should think about system boundaries, relevant for evaluating long-horizon capex and architecture bets by hyperscalers and interconnect suppliers.
insights.locator: Co-packaged optics displacing pluggable modules for scale-up and scale-out links
